Framing is wide so the subject is hard to read on small screens; audio level dips and there's no distinct sound cue.","suggestion":"Recut/re-shoot the opening so the value is explicit in 0–2s: use a tight close‑up, big readable caption (large sans‑serif, high contrast), and a loud audio cue or voice‑over stating the benefit. Start on an action or surprising visual, add a 0.25s sound punch on frame 1, and cut to a 1–2s visual that proves the hook. Keep motion simple (push in / quick jump cut) to maximize retention on mobile."}],"educationalResources":[{"topic":"YouTube Creator Academy — Shorts & Hooks","url":"https://creatoracademy.youtube.com/"},{"topic":"How to Hook Viewers Quickly (InVideo guide)","url":"https://invideo.io/blog/how-to-hook-viewers/"},{"topic":"Short‑form video best practices (Adobe Express)","url":"https://www.adobe.com/express/learn/video/short-form-video-tips"}],"nextSteps":["Reshoot 0–5s: film a close‑up with the on‑screen benefit spoken in one sentence, add a 0.25s audio punch at 0s, and display a single large caption that matches the spoken hook.","Create two variant opens (A/B): Variant A = bold visual + voice hook; Variant B = question + text overlay. Upload both and compare retention after 24–48 hours.","Add subtitles (editable text overlay) and a high‑contrast thumbnail frame pulled from the 0–3s mark.","Watch the three linked resources and implement one lighting/frame adjustment and one sound cue change before the next upload."],"meta":{"model":"gpt-5-mini","duration":80,"attemptsLeft":2}}
cache.ab082e96ddc23b4652baf634ea49ba39: {"items":[{"startSec":0,"endSec":1,"issue":"Early frames (thumbnails at ~0.06–0.97s) show busy textured backgrounds, low subject contrast and no clear visual hook in the first second — the composition reads cluttered on small mobile screens.","suggestion":"Open with a single, high-contrast focal element (center-crop if a face/object exists), shorten the first cut to a 0.5–1s hook, add a large, bold one-line title overlay and boost brightness/contrast so the subject reads on small screens."},{"startSec":1,"endSec":2,"issue":"Later frames (~1.1–1.94s) show rapid visual change and busy motion; pacing and continuity feel uneven and there may be motion blur or unstable framing when viewers expect a payoff.","suggestion":"Stabilize/lock the framing for the payoff moment (1–2s), slow the motion slightly or use a short hold on the key frame, add a clear caption for accessibility, and pick a clean thumbnail from a high-contrast frame (0–1s) for click-through."}],"educationalResources":[{"topic":"3‑second hooks for short video","url":"https://blog.hootsuite.com/how-to-hook-viewers-in-3-seconds/"},{"topic":"Thumbnail design & best practices","url":"https://www.canva.com/learn/video-thumbnails/"},{"topic":"YouTube Shorts: editing & format tips","url":"https://creatoracademy.youtube.com/page/lesson/shorts"}],"nextSteps":["Export a 1.0–1.5s version highlighting your strongest frame and test it as the thumbnail.","Re-edit 0–1s to create a single clear hook (center subject, bold title, +10–20% contrast).","Stabilize the 1–2s payoff frame, add a 2–3 word caption, and A/B test engagement on mobile."],"meta":{"model":"gpt-5-mini","duration":2,"attemptsLeft":1,"frameCount":32,"frameAssumptionIntervalSec":0}}
